old:
Charge-transfer analysis estimates input-power scale, and the resonant equivalent circuit estimates active-cycle gain and phase. Clamp timing and burst transitions require a switched model; efficiency and temperature additionally require calibrated loss and thermal models.

The supplied LTspice circuits describe the predecessor rectifier. Supplied magnetic measurements provide the inductance and transformer parameters used in Chapter~\ref{ch:analysis}. Their application to the prototype accounts for the changed topology and installed components.

A prototype model must predict bus ripple, turn-on current, packet energy, and the response to component or command changes. Matched turn-on-current and packet-energy measurements are still needed to check it.
new:
The charge-transfer calculation estimates the input-power scale, while the resonant equivalent circuit estimates active-cycle gain and phase. The supplied LTspice circuits describe the predecessor rectifier, and the given magnetic measurements provide the inductance and transformer parameters used in Chapter~\ref{ch:analysis}. The calculations account for the prototype's changed topology and installed components.

A switched prototype model is needed to examine clamp timing and burst transitions and to predict bus ripple, turn-on current, packet energy, and the response to component or command changes. Matched turn-on-current and packet-energy measurements are still needed to check it. Efficiency and temperature prediction also require calibrated loss and thermal models.
reason: Groups calculations and supplied inputs before relating the unfinished switched model to the quantities and calibration it needs.
facts_preserved: Predecessor LTspice circuits, magnetic measurements, changed topology and components, matched measurements and loss/thermal calibration.

old:
Three time scales govern operation: carrier-scale phase, clamp timing, and energy per active cycle; burst-scale average transfer; and line-cycle storage imbalance in the DC link and secondary capacitors. The model must resolve all three time scales.

Nominal series resonance is near \SI{0.989}{\mega\hertz}. Turn-on phase also depends on magnetizing current, pump current, and rectifier state, which must be included in commutation prediction.

Calibration requires matched input and secondary demand, followed by separate comparisons of voltage envelopes and switching waveforms. Mean VBUS agreement alone does not validate bulk ripple or commutation current. Chapter~\ref{ch:results} reports these quantities separately.
new:
The model must resolve carrier-scale phase, clamp timing, and energy per active cycle, as well as average transfer over each burst and the line-cycle energy imbalance in the DC link and secondary capacitors. Nominal series resonance is near \SI{0.989}{\mega\hertz}, but turn-on phase also depends on magnetizing current, pump current, and rectifier state.

Calibration requires matched input and secondary demand, followed by separate comparisons of voltage envelopes and switching waveforms. This checks bulk ripple and commutation current as well as mean VBUS. Chapter~\ref{ch:results} reports these quantities separately.
reason: Connects the time scales to physical quantities and explains what waveform comparison checks.
facts_preserved: Three operating time scales, nominal resonance, phase dependencies, matched demand and separate comparisons.

old:
Magnetic temperature depends on winding, core, and terminal losses and thermal coupling from GaN devices, rectifiers, auxiliary supplies, copper, and airflow. The thermal limit cannot be predicted from inductance and turns ratio alone.

The images in \cref{sec:method-thermal,sec:res-thermal} compare surface-temperature patterns at tested outputs. They do not separate core and winding losses or resolve internal winding maxima. Continuous output must be checked by recording temperature over time on the tested assembly.
new: Magnetic temperature depends on winding, core, and terminal losses, as well as heat transferred from the GaN devices, rectifiers, auxiliary supplies, and copper and removed by airflow. The images in \cref{sec:method-thermal,sec:res-thermal} compare surface-temperature patterns at tested outputs, but do not separate core and winding losses or resolve internal winding maxima. Temperatures must be recorded over time on the tested assembly to check continuous output.
reason: Connects thermal paths to the images and measurement needed for sustained operation.
facts_preserved: Thermal paths, tested-output images, unresolved core and winding losses and internal maxima, temperature history.
